artifacts.summary: Verifies the validate-no-task-references.sh regex gap, surveys the literature test harness shape and the lean sorry census tool's cross-check design, flags an existing but divergent core-scripts test precedent (test-task-lock-reap.sh), and recommends a tooling+method deliverable shape with a scope-based test-harness-location rule.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/, an isolated shell-test pattern already exists (test-task-lock-reap.sh): build a throwaway mktemp -d root mimicking the real specs/ tree, copy the actual production script byte-for-byte into it (never mock/stub), and run PASSED/FAILED counter assertions against it. This zero-instrumentation approach avoids adding testability hooks to production scripts and is directly reusable for testing other core scripts (e.g. census tooling).

The literature extension mixes two test-shape conventions by scope, not arbitrarily: narrow single-script fixture-driven regression suites live under scripts/tests/ (test-literature-convert.sh + generate-test-fixtures.py), while a broad end-to-end pipeline suite (test-lit-pipeline.sh) stays flat in scripts/. When choosing a test harness location for a new core script, prefer this scope-based split (narrow->tests/ subdir, broad/pipeline->flat) over blanket copying either shape.

hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh's task-number regex \b[Tt]asks?[[:space:]]+[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?\b requires literal whitespace as the separator, so task-788, task_788, and Task #788 are all invisible to it despite hyphenated task-N forms being a documented, sanctioned convention elsewhere (git branch names in rules/git-workflow.md and rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md's own stated exception). Any future regex meant to catch 'task N' style references anywhere in this repo should use a separator class like [[:space:]_#-]+ (or an explicit alternation) rather than assuming whitespace-only separators, and should consider a parallel Phase N alternative since no existing hook covers Phase references at all.
